flawed_step: Assuming every vertex has positive in-degree, repeatedly choosing an in-neighbor only guarantees a directed cycle of length at most 5, not at most 3. Thus the hypothesis does not yield a contradiction.
counterexample: Let V={1,2,3,4,5} and A={(1,2),(2,3),(3,4),(4,5),(5,1)}. This loopless digraph is a directed 5-cycle. Every vertex has in-degree exactly 1, so it has no vertex of in-degree 0. Its only directed cycle has length 5, hence it contains no directed cycle of length at most 3.
assessment_summary: The proof attempt fails when trying to turn minimum in-degree at least 1 into a cycle of length at most 3. The explicit directed 5-cycle satisfies every hypothesis but violates the conclusion.
